rules.sentence: Several other nonspecific skin manifestations are seen in SLE.
Bullous lupus is a subepidermal bullous dermatosis mediated by autoantibodies against collagen VII.
They tend to occur on the face, upper torso, neck, and axillary flexures and do not leave scars but may leave dyspigmentation.[16]
Bullous lupus can correlate with more severe systemic lupus manifestations.
